newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends sharply down on funds, meal down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends sharply down on funds, meal down.

text.p: Heavy commodity fund sales in CBOT soyoil futures pushed that market to a sharply lower close, and soymeal futures also settled lower.
Commodity funds sold an estimated 5,000 lots of soyoil on the day, pit sources said.
Heavy losses in soybean futures also weighed on both the soymeal and soyoil futures, traders said. CBOT May soybeans ended down 10-3/4 at $8.31-3/4 per bushel.
Market concerns about an outbreak of hoof and mouth disease in Taiwan seemed to moderate somewhat on Monday, and that sentiment supported soymeal prices.
Some traders speculated that the loss in demand for feed from Taiwanese hogs would be replaced by an increase in hog production in the U.S.
"We'll step in where Taiwan left off," said one CBOT floor trader. "If Taiwan doesn't produce the pork, we will."
On Friday, soymeal was under pressure from ideas that the disease outbreak would shut-off demand for feed from Taiwan, traders said.
CBOT soymeal ended down $1.00 to $4.70 per ton, with May down $3.00 at $274.40. Soyoil futures ended down 0.30 to 0.55, with May down 0.55 at $23.85 cent per pound.
